drafted_from: tool:see-if-my-copies-are-in-step's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart", with {"thing_type":"note"}. It runs tool:see-if-my-copies-are-in-step and answers {"devices":[],"versions":[],"other_kinds":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (setting, kept-apart, [object Object]) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart", and give it thing_type (The kind of record whose versions to read or settle (one kind per call; other_kinds names the rest)).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:see-if-my-copies-are-in-step and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads your device rows (setting:catch_up_devices) and every record two copies changed apart (kept-apart records) of the kind you name as thing_type, and answers devices (each device's state, waiting changes and when it last caught up; a copy of your records you send in positions is shown once, as the device that named it or as a copy of its own) and versions (each record kept apart: the record as it is now first, then one side per other version, with the words of its keep button).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: setting (records:read); kept-apart (records:list, records:read); [object Object] (records:read).
